proposal.name: Run Python checks with application dependencies

plan.name: Run Python checks with application dependencies
plan.summary: Build and reuse an application image from project-root requirements.txt and its recursive local requirement and constraint files, using the existing digest-pinned Python base on linux/amd64, without rewriting application inputs or falling back after an installation failure. This first slice accepts PyPI wheel requirements with names, versions, extras, markers and pip hashes, rejects source distributions, URLs, VCS, editable or local packages, environment substitutions and index overrides, and keys reuse on the complete recipe and every referenced input. Select the image once for Python tests, conformance and larger-bound runs, keep Nagini separate, and include canonical input hashes and resolved wheel names, versions, filenames and SHA-256 hashes in JSON and Markdown receipts and their fingerprints; cached images retain their actual resolution, while a fresh build of unpinned requirements may resolve differently. Add acceptance coverage with a referenced-file fixture and an opt-in real Docker run of a small third-party package, and update SPEC.md and README to describe supported forms, offline execution and fingerprints that agree only for the same effective environment. The merger must record the dependency-policy decision and cite it with the existing grounding decisions in changed SPEC bullets under D-0122; attaching this reusable environment evidence to component receipts remains later work because the base branch has only component inventory, while Python existing-code discovery and contract checks remain subsequent issues on #210.

tests.name: TestPythonDependencyRecipeCoversReferencedInputs
tests.says: The recipe covers the recursive requirement and constraint closure, is independent of checkout location and unrelated source, and accepts the documented wheel requirement syntax without changing input files.

tests.name: TestPythonDependenciesRejectUnaccountedInputs
tests.says: Unsupported requirement sources, escaping or symlinked paths, missing references and reference cycles fail before any dependency installation can run.

tests.name: TestPythonDependencyImagesBuildReuseAndRunOffline
tests.says: A dependency image is built once and reused with its recorded wheel provenance, referenced constraints invalidate it, and Python checks use it offline; INVARIANT_PYTHON_DEPS_REAL=1 additionally exercises the same fixture against real Docker and PyPI.

tests.name: TestPythonDependencyFailuresDoNotFallBack
tests.says: Installation failure or missing or malformed resolved artifact evidence prevents Python execution and produces an actionable error rather than a standard-library fallback.

tests.name: TestPythonGateRecordsAndReusesApplicationEnvironment
tests.says: The gate records the environment used by tests and conformance, reuses it one size larger, leaves Nagini's pinned verifier independent, and preserves projects without requirements.

tests.name: TestPythonReceiptIdentifiesResolvedDependencies
tests.says: The receipt shows the Python application base, recipe and resolved artifact evidence separately from Nagini.

tests.name: TestPythonFingerprintTracksResolvedDependencies
tests.says: Dependency evidence survives JSON receipts and changes the fingerprint when effective inputs, platform or resolved artifacts change.

usage.summary: Wrote `plan.json` and seven acceptance tests covering Python dependency images, offline execution, caching, receipts, and documentation updates. The first check passed; `repo/` is unchanged, and the plan records deferred component work and the merger’s required decision.
